answer: Per-identity cost sink. Each agent identity gets a reusable work credential that only accrues value through completed tasks paid by counterparties; the credential's pearl score rises with settled volume and is checked before matching. Cloning forces the attacker to fund fresh credentials through real jobs first, so each new identity costs the same labor as earning one honestly along the river of settlements. A fable of easy duplication fails because unearned credentials stay locked at zero.
